sources.entry: Limbas - Database framework for creating database-driven business applications. As a graphical database frontend, it enables the efficient processing of data stocks and the flexible development of comfortable database applications. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: Limbas is a low-code, PHP-based graphical database front-end for building database-driven business applications.
summary.what_it_does: Limbas is described as a low-code database framework that provides a graphical front-end for processing data stocks and building database applications with little programming knowledge. It supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, MSSQL, SAP MaxDB, and Oracle as backing databases. The README lists requirements of a Linux server, Apache, PHP 8+, and PDO/unixODBC. Installation options include a web installer, a Docker setup, or a manually extracted release package whose document root must point to the "public" directory. Updates are done by backing up and replacing the limbas_src, vendor, and assets folders.
use_cases: build internal business applications without much coding
graphical front-end for managing database records
self-hosted data entry and database frontend
run database applications on a web server with PHP
how_to_run: Option 1: Use the web installer on a webspace (downloads the latest package and redirects to the installer; internet required)
Option 2: Start via Docker (see Limbas Docker documentation)
Option 3: Upload openlimbas_X.X.tar.gz to an empty directory on the server and extract it
Point the domain root to the 'public' directory
Open Limbas in a browser and follow the installation page
Sign in with the default credentials after setup
notable: Low-code approach to building database-driven business applications
Supports five database backends including Oracle and SAP MaxDB
Multiple install paths: web installer, Docker, or release package
Maintained by LIMBAS GmbH with online docs, demo server, and forum
caveats: Requires a Linux server with Apache and PHP 8+ and PDO/unixODBC
Web installer requires an internet connection
Updates require manually backing up and replacing folders
